title: MPSC exam aspirants protest in Pune demanding the commission chairman's resignation

tea.why: Aspirants allege paper leaks and repeated delays in Maharashtra Public Service Commission recruitment exams.
tea.want: Resignation of the MPSC chairman, more transparency, and a say over the exam format (objective vs descriptive).
tea.changed: Oct 5: protests entered their sixth day at three Pune sites; Raj Thackeray was due to visit and Rahul Gandhi may follow.

summary: Candidates preparing for Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) exams have protested in Pune since about September 30, with demonstrations at three locations. Their main demand is the resignation of the commission's chairman amid allegations of paper leaks; groups also disagree among themselves over whether the Main exam should be objective or descriptive. Politicians from several parties have visited: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut and Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke backed the chairman's removal on October 4, and Raut called the site 'the Jantar Mantar of Maharashtra'. Some protesters heckled MP Omraje Nimbalkar over his switch to the Shinde-led Shiv Sena. MNS chief Raj Thackeray was scheduled to join on October 5, and NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said Rahul Gandhi may meet aspirants on October 7 or 8.
demands: Decision on objective or descriptive exam format
response: No response from the state government or the MPSC is reported in these sources; Rohit Pawar urged the government to decide on the chairman's resignation.

crowd.text: thousands of students from across Maharashtra, according to Sanjay Raut

updates.text: Sanjay Raut and Abhijeet Dipke visited and demanded the chairman's removal.
Some protesters heckled MP Omraje Nimbalkar on the fifth day of the protest.
Raj Thackeray was scheduled to join; Rahul Gandhi may visit on Oct 7 or 8.
